clue.text: Round figure is Crosophile's first of three

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: Crosophile is the setter, so the setter's is MY
a figure is a number, here one

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that a round number is the first of three of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is the song line 'One for the money, two for the show, three to get ready': this answer is what the first count is for.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme that opens the theme song, the first count is 'one for' this word, cash.

clue.text: 18 might be impossible if short of shillings and pence (2 of 3)

indicators.note: might be says the letters could be rearranged into something else
short of says some letters are missing from the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: Getting ready would be impossible without any shillings and pence, a plea for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one S and one P out of IMPOSSIBLE and rearrange the remaining IMOSIBLE. '(2 of 3)' marks this as the second of three synonyms for 18, GET READY.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise troops or resources is to make them prepared for action, a synonym of getting set.

clue.text: Respect, manners, standards, missing from the outset? The usual behaviour!

parts.note: something missing is absent, as in having no money: NO

indicators.note: from the outset takes the opening letter of each of the three listed words

explanation.surface: A grumble that respect, manners and standards have been absent from the start, sarcastically called usual behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are the accepted standards of conduct that people ordinarily follow in a society.

clue.text: To scream "That hurt!" is cowardly

parts.note: to scream is to shout loudly, yell
OW is the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that screaming at a little pain is a coward's act.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal slang for lacking courage, as in having a yellow streak.

clue.text: Sad and moved, say, by love in the lady's song of 1Ac, 13 and 18

parts.note: to feel sad is to feel blue

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: moved from side to side, swayed

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the lady's, read as 'the lady is', gives SHE'S
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sad and moving love song sung by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is Carl Perkins's 'Blue Suede Shoes', famously covered by Elvis, which opens 'One for the money, two for the show, three to get ready': 1 across, 13 and 18.
explanation.definitionFit: This rock and roll standard is the song whose opening lyric counts off money, show and getting ready.

clue.text: Some matter I brought up that covers a Catholic priest

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
some says only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A worry about some matter raised that concerns a Catholic priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads as raising a subject; the 'b' of 'brought' is part of the hidden run, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap with ridges worn by Roman Catholic clergy, so it covers the priest's head.

clue.text: No luck with a fantastic 13 (1 of 2)

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone without luck puts on a fantastic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is SHOW; '(1 of 2)' marks this as the first of two synonyms for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncloak something is to reveal it, which is to display it openly.

clue.text: Wine grape? With no smell I might be mistaken

indicators.note: a mistaken arrangement means the letters are out of their right order

explanation.surface: A taster with no sense of smell admits they might misidentify a wine grape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sémillon is a white wine grape grown in Bordeaux and used in Sauternes.

clue.text: Former partner sat with nothing special in this area in the upper circle

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
nothing is zero, the letter O
in this area means here

explanation.surface: An ex-partner sat around in the theatre's upper circle with nothing special happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper circle' suggests the theatre balcony; it is the outermost shell of the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The exosphere is the highest layer of the atmosphere, encircling the planet at the top.

clue.text: Correct from the first person up to the last

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the first person pronoun is me
the last is the end

explanation.surface: Instructions to correct a text from the first person through to the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, a synonym used by editors.

clue.text: Criminal in fret returning unfriendly look when stopped

indicators.note: returning says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to fret is to chafe or rub

indicators.note: stopped means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an unfriendly look is a glare

explanation.surface: A criminal, worried and caught, shoots a hostile look back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RUB into BUR; 'when stopped' drops the final E of GLARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: 18 is mostly manure and earth (1 of 3)

indicators.note: mostly means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: compost is rotted organic matter used, like manure, to feed soil
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A gardener's remark that a preparation is mostly manure and soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is GET READY; '(1 of 3)' marks this as the first of three synonyms for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose yourself is to calm and prepare yourself for what is coming.

clue.text: Is it used to catch young female duck?

parts.note: a lass is a girl, a young female
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question whether something is used to trap a young female duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young female duck' looks like a duckling; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope thrown to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: Maybe Anthony or Joanna took degree dressed scruffily

parts.note: Anthony Trollope and Joanna Trollope are both English novelists

explanation.surface: A novelist named Anthony or Joanna earned a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolloped is a dialect verb meaning slopped about in untidy clothes, like a slattern.

clue.text: Surgeon's first seen with MO in second of three

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is the method of doing something: the how

explanation.surface: A surgeon is first seen with the medical officer in the second of three.
explanation.walkthrough: MO looks like a medical officer; here it is modus operandi. In the theme song, two is 'for the' this word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song's opening count, the second line is 'two for the' spectacle, a performance.

clue.text: Essentially toxic delta area turning into rust

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the middle letters of the word

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: turning says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something poisonous in a river delta zone is turning into rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges INTO to make TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusting is the chemical process by which iron combines with oxygen, a kind of this reaction.

clue.text: 1Ac prohibits restricting free token (1 of 1)

indicators.note: restricting says one piece hems in another

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban, so prohibits gives bans

indicators.note: free says the letters are released from their order

explanation.surface: Money is said to ban a free token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges TOKEN into KNOTE. '(1 of 1)' marks this as the only synonym given for 1 across, MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper currency notes issued by a bank are a form of cash.

clue.text: Originally called on hearing an animal's cry

indicators.note: on hearing says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a horse's cry is a neigh

explanation.surface: An animal was named after the cry people heard it make.
explanation.definitionFit: Née introduces a woman's birth surname, the name she was first given.

clue.text: Climbing aids a number with boring equipment left out

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: out says a letter is left out

parts.note: drills are tools for boring holes

explanation.surface: Climbers' aids number several once the dull kit is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests dull; here it is drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendrils are the thin coiling shoots with which climbing plants grip supports.

clue.text: Obtain 1Ac such as 15 in third of three

parts.note: to obtain is to get
money such as banknotes is informally 'the ready', ready cash

explanation.surface: Collect money such as banknotes in the third of three instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: In the theme song, three is 'to' do this.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's count goes 'three to' prepare, the final step before 'now go'.

clue.text: Avoids returning boxers say being put into teams

indicators.note: being put into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: teams are sides

indicators.note: returning says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: boxer dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: Boxers coming back into teams try to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers look like fighters; they are dogs. 'returning' turns PETS into STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to dodge or evade it.

clue.text: Fruit that's crossed Thailand with a biker ring

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
a Hell's Angel is a biker
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A biker rode across Thailand with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangelo is a hybrid citrus, a tangerine crossed with a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Edited paper about 18 (3 of 3)

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An edited paper about getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is GET READY; '(3 of 3)' marks this as the last of its three synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make ready, the plain synonym.

clue.text: A fair bit taken by cafeteria

indicators.note: a bit taken by the word means a run of letters held within it

explanation.surface: A fair portion has been taken by the cafeteria.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is an outdoor fair or bazaar, often held to raise funds.

clue.text: Put plates out for e.g. rice, sweetcorn …

indicators.note: put ... out asks for the letters to be laid out afresh
out completes put out, showing the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Instructions to set plates out for a meal of rice and sweetcorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice and maize are staple foods, the main starches a diet rests on.

clue.text: To jump on others at metal gig is initially silly and possibly clean mad

definitions.text: To jump on others at metal gig

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word
possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Leaping on others at a heavy metal concert is silly and perhaps crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam-dancing is the moshing style where dancers hurl themselves at one another at punk and metal concerts.

clue.text: See 4
On VHS he recorded a spill

definitions.meaning: someone who records on video tape
a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light candles, as is a slender candle

explanation.surface: A man recorded a spill on video.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who tapes; the other is a slender candle or lighting strip.

clue.text: 13 cycled over after parking (2 of 2)

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the one before
cycled says a letter is moved round from one end to the other

explanation.surface: A show of cycling over after parking the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' moves the final R of OVER to the front, making ROVE. 13 is SHOW; '(2 of 2)' marks the second of its synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something is to demonstrate it, to show it is true.

clue.text: Opening office with fellow going for scripture

indicators.note: going for says one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the school subject of scripture

explanation.surface: An office opens with a fellow leaving for scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is religious instruction, the old British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, especially a body aperture.

clue.text: Ancient storage jar of pharaoh (almost broken) for storage of money

indicators.note: for storage of says one piece is stored inside another
broken says the letters are smashed into a new order
almost says the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A pharaoh's ancient jar, nearly broken, held money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final H of PHARAOH; 'broken' rearranges PHARAO into APHORA, and M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled Greek or Roman jar for wine or oil.

clue.text: Sun tan's done when oiled in ancient section of beach?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as for Sunday

indicators.note: oiled suggests drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A sunbather's tan is done after oiling on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oiled' is slang for drunk, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is rock formed from compacted sand over ages, so it is beach material from long ago.

clue.text: Two letters in print seen by unknown adversary

parts.note: en and em are the printer's units of width, named after the letters N and M
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A rival seen with two letters in print by an unidentified person.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe or opponent, a synonym of adversary.
